text:
A: Hey, Callum, is it? I'm Luke.
B: Yeah, that's me. Alright, mate, nice to meet you.
A: You too. Where are you?
B: Sittingbourne, in Kent. You?
A: Bristol. So there's a bit of motorway between us.
B: Bit of a trek, yeah. Is that a Studio Ghibli thing behind you? My wife's been on at me to watch one of those.
A: It is, yeah, Spirited Away. Oh, you've got to. Start with that one, honestly, or My Neighbour Totoro if you want something gentle. I've got a nine-year-old and she's watched Totoro about forty times.
B: Right, I'll tell Megan. She'll be chuffed I've actually remembered something. What do you do, then?
A: I'm an exec assistant to the MD at an engineering consultancy. Basically I run his life: diary, board meetings, travel, suppliers. And you?
B: Machine operator. Cardboard boxes. I run a flexo printer-folder-gluer, so the board goes in flat and comes out a box, printed and glued. I do the changeovers as well when an order switches. Days one week, backs the next.
A: That's actually quite satisfying, isn't it? Like, you can see the thing at the end.
B: Yeah, that's it, you can see what you've done. I train the new starters and all, which I quite like. I'm trying to get on the maintenance apprenticeship, so I can fix the machines rather than just run them, you know.
A: Oh, nice. That's a smart move. I'm sort of in the same boat, trying to work out the next step. Chief of staff, head of ops, that kind of thing. The trick is making yourself the person nobody can do without, yeah?
B: Yeah, I suppose. I just try and do the job properly and hope someone notices.
A: That works too, to be fair. Probably more honest than mine. Do you do much sport?
B: Five-a-side on Wednesdays with lads from work. I'm at the back, mostly, just stopping people getting through. And I go to Gillingham with my dad now and then.
A: Gillingham! I'm Rovers, sort of by inheritance from my dad. I take my daughter a couple of times a season. I'm more of a parkrun person, really. Horfield Common, when she's at her mum's.
B: Oh, what do you get round in?
A: Erm, on a good day, just under twenty-four. On a bad day I'd rather not say.
B: That's decent, that. I'd be dead. I do a bit of cycling on the Saxon Shore Way, but that's about it.
A: What do you do when you're not knackered from shifts?
B: Garden, mostly. I built raised beds out the back. Tomatoes, chillies, runner beans. I was just talking chillies with Hira in the last one, actually. She grows them too.
A: Ha, nice. I make kimchi, so I'm always after chillies. Well, the flakes, gochugaru. My last batch sort of exploded in the jar.
B: Exploded?
A: Fermentation. The gas builds up. I opened it and it went all up the cupboard. Isla thought it was the best thing ever.
B: That's mental. I'm just chilli and fajitas, me. And a kebab on a Friday from the place by the station.
A: Honestly, a good kebab's hard to beat. Where've you been on holiday lately? I'm always nosing.
B: Lads' weekend in Newcastle last time. And me and Megan do Norfolk or Devon in the summer, a cottage or a caravan. Honeymoon was Crete. I like it all booked and sorted, you know, so nothing goes wrong.
A: Oh, you'd be good at my job, then. I did a month in Japan before my daughter came along, and I'm desperate to do Seoul next, but-
